(Refiles to add dropped title 'I Squared Capital' to seventh paragraph)

DUBLIN, Nov 2 (Reuters) - Global aircraft leasing giant Avolon on Monday announced a new investment platform with I Squared Capital and a subsidiary of the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority (ADIA) expected to initially comprise 22 of the lessor's aircraft valued at $1.4 billion.

Dublin-based Avolon, the world's third-biggest aircraft lessor, said the new joint venture, Constellation Aviation, would provide airlines with access to fleet capacity while giving investors exposure to long-term contracted cash flows.

Aircraft lessors own around half of the world's airline fleet that are in hot demand due to a backlog of plane orders. Avolon agreed its largest ever aircraft order last month, bringing its total number on order to 749, on top of 561 it currently owns.

The $1.4 billion seed portfolio comprises 22 aircraft to be acquired from Avolon with an average age of around five years and leased to 17 airlines in 15 countries, Avolon said.

Avolon, a subsidiary of China's Bohai Leasing Co Ltd, will retain a minority equity interest and serve as Constellation's exclusive aircraft manager and servicer as the platform scales up over time.

A source familiar with the platform said its ambition was to grow the size of the portfolio to $6 billion.

ADIA, one of the world's largest sovereign wealth funds, is the oldest of Abu Dhabi's three major government-controlled funds that invests on behalf of the emirate's government. Miami-headquartered infrastructure investor I Squared Capital manages over $60 billion in assets.

The world's number-two lessor, SMBC Aviation Capital, struck a deal last year that also shared the risk of acquiring U.S.-based rival Air Lease Corp for $7.4 billion with a group of investors via a newly established entity.

(Reporting by Padraic Halpin, editing by Sam Tabahriti)
